title: OLMo: Accelerating the Science of Language Models
authors: D. Groeneveld, I. Beltagy, P. Walsh, et al. (43 authors)
before: Open-weight models shipped weights but withheld data, code and logs.
problem: Weights alone do not let you reproduce or diagnose how a model came to be.
breakthrough: Weights, data, training code, evaluation harness and intermediate checkpoints, all released.
why: The clearest example of genuinely open-source rather than merely open-weight, and the reference for that distinction.
next: OLMo 2 and 3, and continued pressure on what open should mean.
inherits: The vocabulary distinction between open weights and open source.
